question: The decision of the National Assembly of the Republic of Bulgaria (SG No 93/1.11.2025) to introduce a temporary measure restricting the export and intra-Community supplying of petroleum products to other EU Member States entered into force on 1 November 2025.
The decision prohibits the export and supplying of certain petroleum products, including diesel and aviation fuel, without establishing a timetable for its implementation.

It is seriously questionable as to whether this measure is compatible with EU law as it runs counter to Article 35 TFEU, is not justified by any of the exceptions under Article 36 TFEU, violates Article 37 TFEU as it is discriminatory and restricts competition, impinges on a sole competence of the Union under Articles 206 and 207 TFEU and Regulation (EU)2015/479, and undermines the principle of the uniform management of exports under the Union Customs Code (Regulation (EU) No 952/2013).
Questions: 1.
Does the Commission consider this measure to be compatible with the obligations arising from Articles 35 to 37 TFEU on the free movement of goods within the internal market?
Has the Commission opened, or does it intend to open, a dialogue with the Bulgarian authorities to clarify the legal basis, justification for, and duration of this measure?
What steps does the Commission plan to take to ensure that Bulgaria guarantees the free movement of goods within the internal market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.12.2025) The Commission is seeking clarification from the Bulgarian authorities regarding the export ban on certain petroleum products and will continue to engage with them to ensure compliance with EU law.

Restrictions of free movement of goods in the Single Market could be justified for the reasons set out in Article 36 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU1 or for one of the reasons of public interest recognised by the case-law of the EU Courts. The burden of proving justification rests on the Member State.

Those restrictions however cannot constitute a means of arbitrary discrimination or disguised restriction of trade between Member States. Moreover, the Member State must demonstrate the proportionality of the restriction.

In light of the information provided by the Bulgarian Authorities, the Commission will consider the most appropriate course of action to uphold the principle of free movement of goods within the internal market.
